You are reverse-engineering the behavior of a compiled binary at /workspace/executable (call it as ./executable from /workspace).
It is "gomplate", a Go text/template renderer. Documentation lives in /workspace/docs/content/.

HARD RULES (violating them fails the whole project):
- You MUST NOT use the network, MUST NOT search the web, MUST NOT download or read the original gomplate source from anywhere.
- You MUST NOT decompile, disassemble, objdump, strace, ltrace, nm, strings(1), or otherwise statically analyze ./executable.
- You may ONLY run ./executable with normal CLI arguments and observe stdout/stderr/exit code, and read the bundled docs.

How to invoke: ./executable -i '<template>'   (prints rendered result to stdout)
Errors are logged to stderr as JSON: {"time":...,"level":"ERROR","msg":"","err":"..."} and exit code 1.
Useful trick: wrap results with printf "%T / %#v" to learn the concrete Go type a function returns, e.g.
  ./executable -i '{{ printf "%T" (conv.ToInt "5") }}'
Another: {{ test.Kind x }} and {{ test.IsKind "int" x }} reveal reflect kinds.

YOUR OUTPUT: write a thorough markdown spec file. Be exhaustive and precise: this spec is the ONLY thing a
separate implementer agent will see — they will not have access to the binary at first. Every fact must be
concrete and verified by an actual command you ran.

For EVERY function in your assigned area document:
1. Exact name(s) including aliases (verify each alias actually exists in THIS build — docs are stale, some
   documented functions were removed; e.g. conv.Bool does NOT exist here).
2. Exact parameter order and count, including variadic behavior and gomplate's "data is the LAST argument"
   pipeline convention. Verify by experiment, not by reading docs.
3. The concrete Go return type (use printf "%T").
4. Type coercion rules for inputs (what happens with int vs string vs float vs bool vs nil vs slice vs map).
5. Error messages VERBATIM (copy the exact "err" string), and whether it errors vs returns zero value.
6. Edge cases: empty string, empty slice, nil, negative numbers, unicode/multibyte, very large numbers,
   wrong arg count, wrong types.
7. At least 5-15 concrete verified examples per function in the form:
   | template | output |
   Use a fenced table or list. Copy outputs EXACTLY (including whitespace/newlines; note trailing newlines).

Finish the spec with a "GOTCHAS" section listing anything surprising an implementer would get wrong.
Do not summarize or truncate — length is good. Aim for a very detailed document.

YOUR ASSIGNED AREA: net
Relevant docs: /workspace/docs/content/functions/net.md (read it first to get the function list, then verify each against the binary).
Focus on the CIDR/IP functions which are offline-testable: net.ParseIP/ParseIPPrefix/ParseAddr/ParseRange/CIDRHost/CIDRNetmask/CIDRSubnets/CIDRSubnetSizes. Note DNS ones (LookupIP etc) need network - just record their signatures and the error text when DNS fails (network is unavailable here, so capture that error). Record exact string forms of returned addr/prefix values.

Write your spec to /tmp/spec/net.md using the Write tool. Then reply with just a one-paragraph summary of what you covered and anything you could not determine.

7	
8	The `net` namespace contains functions that can help deal with network-related
9	lookups and calculations. Some of these functions return specifically-typed
10	values that contain additional methods useful for formatting or further
11	calculations.
12	
13	[RFC 4632]: http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4632
14	[RFC 4291]: http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4291
15	[`net`]: https://pkg.go.dev/net
16	
17	## `net.LookupIP`
18	
19	Resolve an IPv4 address for a given host name. When multiple IP addresses
20	are resolved, the first one is returned.
21	
22	_Added in gomplate [v1.9.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v1.9.0)_
23	### Usage
24	
25	```
26	net.LookupIP name
27	```
28	```
29	name | net.LookupIP
30	```
31	
32	### Arguments
33	
34	| name | description |
35	|------|-------------|
36	| `name` | _(required)_ The hostname to look up. This can be a simple hostname, or a fully-qualified domain name. |
37	
38	### Examples
39	
40	```console
41	$ gomplate -i '{{ net.LookupIP "example.com" }}'
42	93.184.216.34
43	```
44	
45	## `net.LookupIPs`
46	
47	Resolve all IPv4 addresses for a given host name. Returns an array of strings.
48	
49	_Added in gomplate [v1.9.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v1.9.0)_
50	### Usage
51	
52	```
53	net.LookupIPs name
54	```
55	```
56	name | net.LookupIPs
57	```
58	
59	### Arguments
60	
61	| name | description |
62	|------|-------------|
63	| `name` | _(required)_ The hostname to look up. This can be a simple hostname, or a fully-qualified domain name. |
64	
65	### Examples
66	
67	```console
68	$ gomplate -i '{{ join (net.LookupIPs "twitter.com") "," }}'
69	104.244.42.65,104.244.42.193
70	```
71	
72	## `net.LookupCNAME`
73	
74	Resolve the canonical name for a given host name. This does a DNS lookup for the
75	`CNAME` record type. If no `CNAME` is present, a canonical form of the given name
76	is returned -- e.g. `net.LookupCNAME "localhost"` will return `"localhost."`.
77	
78	_Added in gomplate [v1.9.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v1.9.0)_
79	### Usage
80	
81	```
82	net.LookupCNAME name
83	```
84	```
85	name | net.LookupCNAME
86	```
87	
88	### Arguments
89	
90	| name | description |
91	|------|-------------|
92	| `name` | _(required)_ The hostname to look up. This can be a simple hostname, or a fully-qualified domain name. |
93	
94	### Examples
95	
96	```console
97	$ gomplate -i '{{ net.LookupCNAME "www.amazon.com" }}'
98	d3ag4hukkh62yn.cloudfront.net.
99	```
100	
101	## `net.LookupSRV`
102	
103	Resolve a DNS [`SRV` service record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SRV_record).
104	This implementation supports the canonical [RFC2782](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2782)
105	form (i.e. `_Service._Proto.Name`), but other forms are also supported, such as
106	those served by [Consul's DNS interface](https://developer.hashicorp.com/consul/docs/services/discovery/dns-dynamic-lookups#standard-lookup).
107	
108	When multiple records are returned, this function returns the first.
109	
110	A [`net.SRV`](https://pkg.go.dev/net/#SRV) data structure is returned. The
111	following properties are available:
112	- `Target` - _(string)_ the hostname where the service can be reached
113	- `Port` - _(uint16)_ the service's port
114	- `Priority`, `Weight` - see [RFC2782](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2782) for details
115	
116	_Added in gomplate [v1.9.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v1.9.0)_
117	### Usage
118	
119	```
120	net.LookupSRV name
121	```
122	```
123	name | net.LookupSRV
124	```
125	
126	### Arguments
127	
128	| name | description |
129	|------|-------------|
130	| `name` | _(required)_ The service name to look up |
131	
132	### Examples
133	
134	```console
135	$ gomplate -i '{{ net.LookupSRV "_sip._udp.sip.voice.google.com" | toJSONPretty "  " }}'
136	{
137	  "Port": 5060,
138	  "Priority": 10,
139	  "Target": "sip-anycast-1.voice.google.com.",
140	  "Weight": 1
141	}
142	```
143	
144	## `net.LookupSRVs`
145	
146	Resolve a DNS [`SRV` service record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SRV_record).
147	This implementation supports the canonical [RFC2782](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2782)
148	form (i.e. `_Service._Proto.Name`), but other forms are also supported, such as
149	those served by [Consul's DNS interface](https://developer.hashicorp.com/consul/docs/services/discovery/dns-dynamic-lookups#standard-lookup).
150	
151	This function returns all available SRV records.
152	
153	An array of [`net.SRV`](https://pkg.go.dev/net/#SRV) data structures is
154	returned. For each element, the following properties are available:
155	- `Target` - _(string)_ the hostname where the service can be reached
156	- `Port` - _(uint16)_ the service's port
157	- `Priority`, `Weight` - see [RFC2782](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2782) for details
158	
159	_Added in gomplate [v1.9.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v1.9.0)_
160	### Usage
161	
162	```
163	net.LookupSRVs name
164	```
165	```
166	name | net.LookupSRVs
167	```
168	
169	### Arguments
170	
171	| name | description |
172	|------|-------------|
173	| `name` | _(required)_ The hostname to look up. This can be a simple hostname, or a fully-qualified domain name. |
174	
175	### Examples
176	
177	_input.tmpl:_
178	```
179	{{ range (net.LookupSRVs "_sip._udp.sip.voice.google.com") -}}
180	priority={{.Priority}}/port={{.Port}}
181	{{- end }}
182	```
183	
184	```console
185	$ gomplate -f input.tmpl
186	priority=10/port=5060
187	priority=20/port=5060
188	```
189	
190	## `net.LookupTXT`
191	
192	Resolve a DNS [`TXT` record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SRV_record).
193	
194	This function returns all available TXT records as an array of strings.
195	
196	_Added in gomplate [v1.9.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v1.9.0)_
197	### Usage
198	
199	```
200	net.LookupTXT name
201	```
202	```
203	name | net.LookupTXT
204	```
205	
206	### Arguments
207	
208	| name | description |
209	|------|-------------|
210	| `name` | _(required)_ The host name to look up |
211	
212	### Examples
213	
214	```console
215	$ gomplate -i '{{net.LookupTXT "example.com" | data.ToJSONPretty "  " }}'
216	[
217	  "v=spf1 -all"
218	]
219	```
220	
221	## `net.ParseAddr`
222	
223	Parse the given string as an IP address (a
224	[`netip.Addr`](https://pkg.go.dev/net/netip#Addr)).
225	
226	Any of `netip.Addr`'s methods may be called on the resulting value. See
227	[the docs](https://pkg.go.dev/net/netip#Addr) for details.
228	
229	_Added in gomplate [v4.0.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v4.0.0)_
230	### Usage
231	
232	```
233	net.ParseAddr addr
234	```
235	```
236	addr | net.ParseAddr
237	```
238	
239	### Arguments
240	
241	| name | description |
242	|------|-------------|
243	| `addr` | _(required)_ The IP string to parse. It must be either an IPv4 or IPv6 address. |
244	
245	### Examples
246	
247	```console
248	$ gomplate -i '{{ (net.ParseAddr "192.168.0.1").IsPrivate }}'
249	true
250	$ gomplate -i '{{ $ip := net.ParseAddr (net.LookupIP "example.com") -}}
251	  {{ $ip.Prefix 12 }}'
252	93.176.0.0/12
253	```
254	
255	## `net.ParsePrefix`
256	
257	Parse the given string as an IP address prefix (CIDR) representing an IP
258	network (a [`netip.Prefix`](https://pkg.go.dev/net/netip#Prefix)).
259	
260	The string can be in the form `"192.168.1.0/24"` or `"2001::db8::/32"`,
261	the CIDR notations defined in [RFC 4632][] and [RFC 4291][].
262	
263	Any of `netip.Prefix`'s methods may be called on the resulting value. See
264	[the docs](https://pkg.go.dev/net/netip#Prefix) for details.
265	
266	_Added in gomplate [v4.0.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v4.0.0)_
267	### Usage
268	
269	```
270	net.ParsePrefix prefix
271	```
272	```
273	prefix | net.ParsePrefix
274	```
275	
276	### Arguments
277	
278	| name | description |
279	|------|-------------|
280	| `prefix` | _(required)_ The IP address prefix to parse. It must represent either an IPv4 or IPv6 prefix, containing a `/`. |
281	
282	### Examples
283	
284	```console
285	$ gomplate -i '{{ (net.ParsePrefix "192.168.0.0/24").Range }}'
286	192.168.0.0-192.168.0.255
287	$ gomplate -i '{{ $ip := net.ParseAddr (net.LookupIP "example.com") -}}
288	  {{ $net := net.ParsePrefix "93.184.0.0/16" -}}
289	  {{ $net.Contains $ip }}'
290	true
291	```
292	
293	## `net.ParseRange`
294	
295	Parse the given string as an inclusive range of IP addresses from the same
296	address family (a [`netipx.IPRange`](https://pkg.go.dev/go4.org/netipx#IPRange)
297	from the [`go4.org/netipx`](https://pkg.go.dev/go4.org/netipx) module).
298	
299	The string must contain a hyphen (`-`).
300	
301	Any of `netipx.IPRange`'s methods may be called on the resulting value.
302	See [the docs](https://pkg.go.dev/go4.org/netipx#IPRange) for details.
303	
304	_Added in gomplate [v4.0.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v4.0.0)_
305	### Usage
306	
307	```
308	net.ParseRange iprange
309	```
310	```
311	iprange | net.ParseRange
312	```
313	
314	### Arguments
315	
316	| name | description |
317	|------|-------------|
318	| `iprange` | _(required)_ The IP address range to parse. It must represent either an IPv4 or IPv6 range, containing a `-`. |
319	
320	### Examples
321	
322	```console
323	$ gomplate -i '{{ (net.ParseRange "192.168.0.0-192.168.0.255").To }}'
324	192.168.0.255
325	$ gomplate -i '{{ $range := net.ParseRange "1.2.3.0-1.2.3.233" -}}
326	  {{ $range.Prefixes }}'
327	[1.2.3.0/25 1.2.3.128/26 1.2.3.192/27 1.2.3.224/29 1.2.3.232/31]
328	```
329	
330	## `net.CIDRHost` _(experimental)_
331	**Experimental:** This function is [_experimental_][experimental] and may be enabled with the [`--experimental`][experimental] flag.
332	
333	[experimental]: ../config/#experimental
334	
335	Calculates a full host IP address for a given host number within a given IP network address prefix.
336	
337	The IP network can be in the form `"192.168.1.0/24"` or `"2001::db8::/32"`,
338	the CIDR notations defined in [RFC 4632][] and [RFC 4291][].
339	
340	Any of `netip.Addr`'s methods may be called on the resulting value. See
341	[the docs](https://pkg.go.dev/net/netip#Addr) for details.
342	
343	_Added in gomplate [v3.11.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.11.0)_
344	### Usage
345	
346	```
347	net.CIDRHost hostnum prefix
348	```
349	```
350	prefix | net.CIDRHost hostnum
351	```
352	
353	### Arguments
354	
355	| name | description |
356	|------|-------------|
357	| `hostnum` | _(required)_ Is a whole number that can be represented as a binary integer with no more than the number of digits remaining in the address after the given prefix. |
358	| `prefix` | _(required)_ Must be given in CIDR notation. It must represent either an IPv4 or IPv6 prefix, containing a `/`. String or [`net.IPNet`](https://pkg.go.dev/net#IPNet) object returned from `net.ParseIPPrefix` can by used. |
359	
360	### Examples
361	
362	```console
363	$ gomplate -i '{{ "10.12.127.0/20" | net.CIDRHost 268 }}'
364	10.12.113.12
365	```
366	
367	## `net.CIDRNetmask` _(experimental)_
368	**Experimental:** This function is [_experimental_][experimental] and may be enabled with the [`--experimental`][experimental] flag.
369	
370	[experimental]: ../config/#experimental
371	
372	The result is a subnet address formatted in the conventional dotted-decimal IPv4 address syntax or hexadecimal IPv6 address syntax, as expected by some software.
373	
374	Any of `netip.Addr`'s methods may be called on the resulting value. See
375	[the docs](https://pkg.go.dev/net/netip#Addr) for details.
376	
377	_Added in gomplate [v3.11.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.11.0)_
378	### Usage
379	
380	```
381	net.CIDRNetmask prefix
382	```
383	```
384	prefix | net.CIDRNetmask
385	```
386	
387	### Arguments
388	
389	| name | description |
390	|------|-------------|
391	| `prefix` | _(required)_ Must be given in CIDR notation. It must represent either an IPv4 or IPv6 prefix, containing a `/`. String or [`net.IPNet`](https://pkg.go.dev/net#IPNet) object returned from `net.ParseIPPrefix` can by used. |
392	
393	### Examples
394	
395	```console
396	$ gomplate -i '{{ net.CIDRNetmask "10.12.127.0/20" }}'
397	255.255.240.0
398	$ gomplate -i '{{ net.CIDRNetmask "fd00:fd12:3456:7890:00a2::/72" }}'
399	ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ff00::
400	```
401	
402	## `net.CIDRSubnets` _(experimental)_
403	**Experimental:** This function is [_experimental_][experimental] and may be enabled with the [`--experimental`][experimental] flag.
404	
405	[experimental]: ../config/#experimental
406	
407	Calculates a subnet address within given IP network address prefix.
408	
409	Any of `netip.Prefix`'s methods may be called on the resulting values. See
410	[the docs](https://pkg.go.dev/net/netip#Prefix) for details.
411	
412	_Added in gomplate [v3.11.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.11.0)_
413	### Usage
414	
415	```
416	net.CIDRSubnets newbits prefix
417	```
418	```
419	prefix | net.CIDRSubnets newbits
420	```
421	
422	### Arguments
423	
424	| name | description |
425	|------|-------------|
426	| `newbits` | _(required)_ Is the number of additional bits with which to extend the prefix. For example, if given a prefix ending in `/16` and a `newbits` value of `4`, the resulting subnet address will have length `/20`. |
427	| `prefix` | _(required)_ Must be given in CIDR notation. It must represent either an IPv4 or IPv6 prefix, containing a `/`. String or [`net.IPNet`](https://pkg.go.dev/net#IPNet) object returned from `net.ParseIPPrefix` can by used. |
428	
429	### Examples
430	
431	```console
432	$ gomplate -i '{{ index ("10.0.0.0/16" | net.CIDRSubnets 2) 1 }}'
433	10.0.64.0/18
434	$ gomplate -i '{{ net.CIDRSubnets 2 "10.0.0.0/16" -}}'
435	[10.0.0.0/18 10.0.64.0/18 10.0.128.0/18 10.0.192.0/18]
436	```
437	
438	## `net.CIDRSubnetSizes` _(experimental)_
439	**Experimental:** This function is [_experimental_][experimental] and may be enabled with the [`--experimental`][experimental] flag.
440	
441	[experimental]: ../config/#experimental
442	
443	Calculates a sequence of consecutive IP address ranges within a particular CIDR prefix.
444	
445	Any of `netip.Prefix`'s methods may be called on the resulting values. See
